research_question: Can a literature-supported errorTarget within 1-5% reduce unwanted far-field refinement while retaining the horizontal crack-path refinement region?

literature_target.digitization_metadata: IMAGE_DERIVED_APPROXIMATION (Visual estimation from Fig. 5(b) and Fig. 6(a) colormaps with +/- 20% uncertainty)

scientific_findings: Increasing errorTarget from 1.0% to 2.0-3.0% substantially suppresses global overrefinement, reducing total element counts by 74.7% (14,662) and 88.2% (6,835).

At errorTarget = 2.0%, the mesh element count (14,662) is numerically close to the published count (13,941), but total count is secondary; the spatial morphology remains a diffuse diamond/hourglass-shaped refinement zone (band width w = 0.763 mm at x=0.5 mm) rather than the published narrow rectangular horizontal crack-path corridor (w ~ 0.10 mm).

At errorTarget = 3.0%, although refinement localizes strongly around the initial crack tip (bbox y-span = 0.175 mm for h <= 3 um), the ligament bandwidth at x = 0.7 mm is zero (w = 0.0 mm), failing to maintain horizontal right-ligament refinement ahead of the crack path.
At errorTarget = 5.0%, refinement is overly restricted to the singular crack tip (w = 0.142 mm at x=0.5 mm, w = 0 mm for x >= 0.6 mm), leaving the crack path at coarse nominal sizing.

The 2%, 3%, and 5% cases are sensitivity study settings rather than literal main-benchmark settings (the principal Pandey-Kumar benchmark specifies l0 = 0.0075 mm, nominal h = 0.02 mm, and Listing-1 errorTarget = 1.0; their sensitivity section changes surrounding parameters such as l0 = 0.01 mm and errorTarget = 5).

Preserved sensitivity finding: Increasing errorTarget systematically reduces broad refinement, but no tested errorTarget value simultaneously reproduces a narrow horizontal band and keeps the right ligament sufficiently refined under whole-domain UNIFORM_ERROR remeshing.
